5c452c65-eb85-4132-91f8-fa3d67dde008.description: Grilled pork or chicken marinated in a special mixture of vinegar, garlic, and local spices, wrapped in banana leaves to infuse an earthy aroma.
ingredients: 1 kg pork (belly or shoulder) or native chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup vinegar (native cane or tuba vinegar)
procedure: In a large bowl, combine the meat with garlic, ginger, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Cover and marinate for at least 1 hour or overnight in the refrigerator.
Wrap a few pieces of marinated meat tightly in clean banana leaves.
Grill over hot charcoal for 10–15 minutes per side until cooked through.
Remove from grill, unwrap, and serve hot with steamed rice.

8e01cbcc-3f34-47f3-92fa-38403c7ad1d9.description: A traditional chicken soup distinguished by its coconut water broth, giving it a light, subtly sweet taste with aromatic notes of ginger and lemongrass.
ingredients: 2 lbs chicken (native darag chicken ideal), cut into serving pieces
1 medium green papaya or chayote, cubed
2 stalks lemongrass, white parts only, crushed
Fish sauce or salt to taste
procedure: Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in cooking oil.
Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the young coconut water and add lemongrass; bring to a boil and simmer until chicken is tender.
Add the papaya or chayote and coconut meat; cook until vegetables are soft.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and peppercorns.
Add moringa leaves and chili peppers; turn off heat and let the residual heat cook the leaves.
Serve hot.

78e4a165-1ef0-4476-9f53-1e7daadad44e.description: A delicacy featuring native chicken and aromatics wrapped tightly in banana leaves and slow-cooked to create a flavorful, steaming broth.
ingredients: 1/2 native chicken, deboned and cut into bite-size chunks
procedure: Place chicken in a pot with onion, tomatoes, MSG (optional), and salt. Add enough water to cover.
Boil for 30 minutes to 1 hour depending on the age of the chicken.
Prepare the wrapper by lining a bowl with saba banana leaves.
Place the boiled chicken and broth into the leaf-lined bowl.
Gather the ends of the leaves and tie securely with a string to prevent dripping.
Steam the wrapped package for a few minutes to infuse flavors.
Remove from heat, unwrap, and serve.

1abd40bb-0216-42cf-a865-2dbf4babd0c0.description: A sweet, crunchy puffed rice snack bound together by a muscovado sugar syrup known as 'lasaw'.
ingredients: 1/2 to 3/4 cup Muscovado or brown sugar
procedure: Dry cooked rice in the sun for 4 hours, then deep fry for a few seconds until it puffs. Drain well.
In a pan, melt sugar over low heat. Add butter and calamansi juice, stirring constantly into a thick syrup.
Quickly mix in the puffed rice and toasted sesame seeds until thoroughly coated.
Transfer to a greased pan; flatten and compress firmly while warm.
Let cool for 30 minutes until hardened, then cut into squares.

f93fadd6-a8dc-4447-807e-bdde9fa2d3b1.description: A savory dish of ground freshwater shrimp and grated coconut wrapped in young taro leaves and simmered in coconut milk.
ingredients: 1/2 kg Freshwater Shrimps (hipon), shelled and pounded
procedure: Mix shrimp paste, grated coconut, ginger, garlic, and onion in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Place a spoonful of the mixture into the center of 1-2 gabi leaves and roll into a tight packet.
Arrange the packets closely in a pot.
Pour coconut milk over the packets and add chilies.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 20-30 minutes until the milk reduces to a thick sauce and leaves are tender.
Serve hot with rice.

a3352a39-7a0e-45b2-9bd5-dc902539b73f.description: Fresh whole fish marinated in a simple mixture of vinegar and aromatics, then grilled over charcoal.
procedure: Mix vinegar, garlic, salt, and pepper to create the marinade.
Marinate the fish for 20–30 minutes.
Preheat the grill with charcoal.
Grill the fish until fully cooked on both sides.
Serve hot with rice and a dipping sauce of vinegar, garlic, and chili.

b3029618-6ed5-4ec7-aae3-82566f04236f.description: A spicy chicken dish cooked in a rich, red chili-infused broth with coconut milk, a specialty of the Altavas community.
ingredients: 1 whole native chicken, cut into serving pieces
1/2 cup red chili peppers (siling labuyo), pounded
procedure: Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in cooking oil until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil, then simmer until chicken is tender.
Add the pounded chilies and coconut cream.
Stir in vinegar and season with salt.
Simmer for another 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

45ce32cd-48ac-4116-b4bc-256a42078300.description: A traditional sweet soup made from kamang (shellfish), bayabas (guava), and lasaw (muscovado sugar syrup), a unique Balete specialty.
ingredients: 1 kg kamang (freshwater shellfish or mussels), cleaned
procedure: Boil water with ginger in a pot.
Add kamang and cook until shells open.
Add sliced guavas and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in muscovado sugar until dissolved.
Add glutinous rice balls if using.
Simmer until soup thickens slightly.
Serve warm as a sweet snack or dessert.

1cf1a39a-4de4-4d28-a4d1-674b5dd39cd0.description: Fish cooked in vinegar with ginger and spices, a Banga specialty that showcases the town's abundance of fresh seafood.
ingredients: 1 kg fresh fish (talakitok or lapu-lapu), cut into thick slices
procedure: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger.
Add fish slices and brown lightly.
Pour in vinegar and bring to a boil without stirring.
Add fish stock, chilies, peppercorns, and salt.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until fish is cooked and sauce reduces.
Serve with steamed rice.

f320c114-706c-4370-9d31-9d88dcf2cd2d.description: Fresh fish wrapped in banana leaves with coconut milk, lemongrass, and aromatics, steamed to perfection - a coastal Buruanga specialty.
procedure: Clean the fish and make shallow cuts on both sides.
Season with salt, pepper, and garlic.
Place fish on banana leaves lined with lemongrass and ginger.
Pour coconut milk over the fish and wrap tightly.
Steam over medium heat for 30-40 minutes.
Open carefully and serve hot with rice.

bd61aafa-07a9-40d3-888b-ce0f62906b08.description: The capital's signature dish - small fish (danggit or bulinaw) cooked in vinegar with ginger and garlic, a breakfast staple of Kalibo.
ingredients: 1/2 kg small fish (danggit or bulinaw), cleaned
procedure: Heat oil and sauté garlic until golden.
Add ginger and onion, sauté until fragrant.
Add fish and brown lightly on both sides.
Pour in vinegar and water, bring to a boil.
Add peppercorns, salt, and chilies.
Simmer for 15 minutes until fish is tender.
Serve hot with rice; pairs well with fried rice.

3f07ba70-d2d1-4051-9001-a7b558a7e04f.description: Spiced ground meat mixed with grated coconut, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed - a Libacao specialty perfect for baon.
procedure: Mix ground meat with onion, garlic, ginger, and spices.
Add grated coconut and mix thoroughly.
Season with vinegar, fish sauce, salt, and pepper.
Place portions onto banana leaf squares.
Roll and fold securely like a small packet.
Steam for 30-40 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot or pack for travel.

527a74a0-c64c-4005-a322-90fe7242b7a1.description: A sour soup made with fresh seafood from the waters near Boracay, using native kamias and tomatoes for that perfect tangy flavor.
procedure: Boil water with tomatoes, ginger, and onion.
Add kaimitos or tamarind and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the seafood, starting with fish, then shrimp and squid.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until seafood is done.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Add kangkong and gabi leaves, cook for 2 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

dad79933-425f-4cb2-bcc6-09012ceb7d6b.description: Crispy fried pork internals (intestines) seasoned with salt and vinegar, a Malinao specialty that's perfect as a snack or appetizer.
procedure: Clean pork intestines multiple times with vinegar and salt.
Boil in salted water until tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Cut into bite-sized pieces and season with garlic, pepper, and salt.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with calamansi dipping sauce.

0efe5991-6c48-442e-b192-9403cde1c349.description: A hearty noodle soup with rich pork broth, egg noodles, and toppings of chicharon, garlic chips, and green onions - a Nabas comfort food.
procedure: Boil pork bones and belly in water for 2-3 hours until broth is rich.
Season with fish sauce, pepper, and salt.
Cook egg noodles in boiling water until tender.
Place noodles in bowls and ladle hot broth over them.
Top with sliced pork belly, chicharon, garlic chips, and green onions.
Add halved hard-boiled eggs.
Serve piping hot.

ba080844-07b3-4e23-8f00-1f193a1ad261.description: Traditional rice cake made with glutinous rice, coconut milk, and sugar, baked in clay pots with banana leaves - a New Washington specialty.
procedure: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, eggs, and baking powder until smooth.
Line clay pots or baking pan with banana leaves.
Pour batter and top with salted grated coconut.
Bake in hot oven or over coals for 30-40 minutes until golden.
Brush with butter while warm.
Serve sliced, either warm or at room temperature.

acbe190f-2005-4687-9aa3-17f4bbe08f72.description: Sweetened coconut strips dried under the sun, a Numancia treat that captures the sweetness of local coconuts.
procedure: Extract coconut meat and cut into thin strips.
Boil water with muscovado sugar until syrup forms.
Add coconut strips and simmer until translucent and coated.
Spread on clean trays or banana leaves.
Dry under direct sunlight for 2-3 days until chewy.
Store in airtight containers.
